nvd.title: NVD key for the agents
nvd.intro: One NVD key for the organisation, kept only in the Central database. The agents ask Central for their NVD data (a request signed like a report), so they use the key without having it. Central remembers the answers (one product asked by many clients is one request to NVD) and keeps NVD's limit for all of them at once. Without a key in Central the agents ask NVD themselves, slowly.

nvd.note: The key cannot be read back from the application, only replaced or removed. NVD ties a key to one requester: this is your organisation's key and Central makes the clients' lookups on its behalf. Needs ovh/nvd.php uploaded.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Manage the encryption key protecting device credentials and TOTP secrets.
security.adminOnly: This section is only available to administrators.
security.keyExplanation: This key protects device passwords, SNMP community strings, and the local emergency account's TOTP secret stored in the local database. Rotating generates a new key and re-encrypts everything with it — the old key stops working.
security.rotateConfirm: This will generate a new key and re-encrypt every password and secret in the database with it. The operation is safe (the old key is only swapped in after all data has been successfully rewritten) but irreversible — continue?
security.backupExplanation: A weekly, encrypted backup of the database, encryption key, and config, sent to OVH — so a lost disk doesn't also mean losing the entire device inventory, credentials, and central access. Requires a configured E2E key (Central → Agent); without it, no backup is sent at all (never unencrypted).

security.backupRestoreHint: To restore: download a backup from the "Central" view → "Backups" button next to the client, then run backend/scripts/restore_backup.py <file> <enc_key>.
security.restoreExplanation: Upload a backup file downloaded from the "Central" view ("Backups" button) and provide the E2E key it was encrypted with — the agent will rebuild its database, credentials, and config from it, then restart automatically.
security.restoreCliHint: If the agent won't start at all (dead disk, fresh install) — this screen can't help, since there's nothing to log into. In that case use backend/scripts/restore_backup.py <file> <enc_key> before launching the app.
security.restoreEncKeyPrefilled: (configured key detected — leave blank to use it)
security.restoreEncKeyFromFile: (key found in file — leave blank to use it)
security.restoreKeyFoundInFile: Found an E2E key bundled with this file — it will be used automatically.
security.restoreConfirm: This will overwrite the ENTIRE local database and agent config with the backup's data, then restart the app. Current data is moved aside (not deleted), but this is otherwise irreversible without manual intervention — continue?
security.restoreStagedSuccess: Backup verified and staged — the agent is restarting now. Refresh the page shortly.
security.restoreFailed: Restore failed — check the file and key.
security.supplyChainExplanation: Weekly scan of backend (pip-audit) and frontend (npm audit) dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs), plus static analysis of our own code (Bandit, ESLint security) for common security bugs — all in the application's own code, not the client's network.

sources.failingTitle: The scan cannot see vulnerabilities: the latest requests to NVD failed.
sources.failingBody: While NVD cannot be reached (no internet, a firewall, an antivirus that replaces HTTPS certificates), results are not updated and what was known before stays as it is.
sources.intro: Vulnerabilities are looked up in NVD (NIST). Without a key NVD answers only a few requests per half minute, so the scan of a larger network takes very long; a free key makes it about ten times faster.
sources.note: The key is stored encrypted on the agent. NVD ties it to one requester: for the agents of different clients it is better to request a separate key (it is free).

cause.unknown: The cause cannot be determined from the available logs
cause.port_link_down: Switch port lost its link (link down)
cause.device_reboot: Network device restart or power loss
cause.firewall_block: Host traffic blocked by the firewall

causeHint.unknown: No network device logged an event related to this outage. Most often the problem is on the host itself (shutdown, sleep, restart, power, OS or network card), or the router does not log such events.
causeHint.port_link_down: The port the host is plugged into briefly lost its link. Check the cable and socket, the host's network card, host power or sleep, and speed negotiation.
causeHint.device_reboot: During the outage the router or switch the host connects through logged a restart or watchdog event. Check that device's power and stability.
causeHint.loop_stp: A loop or STP topology change was detected — traffic was briefly blocked. Look for unplanned links between ports and unmanaged switches.
causeHint.wifi_key_timeout: The host did not finish the key exchange with the access point — usually interference, weak signal or a Wi-Fi security misconfiguration.
causeHint.wifi_weak_signal: The access point disconnected the host because its signal was too weak. Consider moving the host closer, repositioning access points or adjusting the signal threshold.
causeHint.wifi_data_loss: The connection was dropped due to heavy data loss — typically radio interference or an overloaded channel. Consider changing the channel.
causeHint.wifi_deauth: The host was disconnected from Wi-Fi (deauthentication or leaving the network). Check the Wi-Fi card's power saving, roaming between access points and timeout settings.
causeHint.ip_conflict: An IP address conflict or duplicate was detected — two devices may be using the same address. Check static addresses outside the DHCP pool.
causeHint.dhcp_pool_exhausted: The DHCP server could not assign an address. Enlarge the address pool or shorten the lease time.
causeHint.dhcp_ip_changed: The address lease expired or was released and the host's address may have changed. Consider a static lease reservation for this host.
causeHint.firewall_block: A firewall rule was dropping this host's traffic during the outage. Check whether that is intended.

rules.title: Detection rules
rules.subtitle: What the agent detects by itself from the data it already collects. A rule's first run only remembers the present state (it raises nothing), after that it raises one alert per new thing; a closed alert does not come back.
rules.baseline: The first run records the present state as known and reports nothing.

ruledesc.new_device: A device that has never been seen on the network appeared in the inventory. Closing the alert approves it.
ruledesc.new_port: A host with a known set of open ports opened a new one; RDP, SMB, Telnet, databases and the like are rated higher.
ruledesc.new_vuln: A critical or high CVE that was not on the host before: a new CVE for what runs there, or a new host that has one.
ruledesc.mac_changed: An address now belongs to another network card than before: a replaced device, a reused DHCP address, or ARP spoofing.
ruledesc.compliance_regression: A configuration check that passed now fails: a changed setting or a weakened policy.

risk.title: Asset risk
risk.subtitle: Which devices are worst off and why: open alerts, vulnerabilities, an operating system out of support, missing updates, failed hardening checks, risky services and devices with a possible factory password, put together into one number (at most 100).
risk.empty: No device has anything against it right now.

factor.lifecycle: Operating system out of support or near its end

risk.noDetail: No problems reported for this device (or it is outside the 60 most exposed ones the agent sends the detail for).

avail.title: Device availability
avail.subtitle: Whether the devices answer, since when, and how long they were away. A device behind a switch that is down is "unreachable": a consequence of one fault, not a separate fault.
avail.watchHint: Automatic: network gear, servers and everything something else is attached to. A workstation can be added by hand.
avail.empty: No devices are monitored yet. They appear once the inventory and the network map are ready.
avail.note: Checked every minute: an answer to ping or to one of a few TCP ports. Availability counts from the first check; an outage is the time it was down or unreachable.

svc.title: Business services and SLA
svc.subtitle: A service is what people use ("mail", "accounting", "the shop"), described as the equipment it needs. Its state follows from the availability of that equipment, and the SLA is counted from its history.

cfg.title: Router configuration history
cfg.subtitle: What was changed on a router, when, and what it was before: the versions of the configuration of every MikroTik with a comparison of any two. A configuration change is an alert of the device.
cfg.empty: No MikroTik routers with an assigned credential.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.subtitle: Questions about the network in plain words: Claude reaches into this agent's data (alerts, risk, inventory, vulnerabilities, availability, configurations, syslog) through read-only tools and answers from it.
ai.thinking: The assistant is checking the data…
ai.placeholder: Ask a question, e.g. which servers are going out of support? (Enter sends, Shift+Enter a new line)

privacy.title: What leaves the organisation
privacy.body: The question and the data the assistant reads with its tools (device names, IP addresses, alert texts, software versions, syslog lines) are sent to the Claude API of Anthropic. Passwords, secrets, keys, SNMP communities, MAC addresses, serial numbers and notes are not sent; texts are cut. The assistant changes nothing. Every question is recorded (who, when, which tools, how many tokens).

syslog.title: Syslog and SNMP traps
syslog.subtitle: Events from devices that cannot run an agent: switches, printers, UPSes, firewalls. The device sends what it logs (syslog) or that something happened (an SNMP trap), and the agent recognises what matters and turns it into alerts.

how.title: How to point the devices at this agent
how.intro: The address of this agent on the network: {{host}}. The device has to be in the inventory (or allow unknown ones).
how.mikrotik: MikroTik: /system logging action add name=mm target=remote remote={{host}} remote-port={{port}} bsd-syslog=yes, then /system logging add topics=system,error,critical,warning,info action=mm
how.cisco: Cisco: logging host {{host}} (default port) and logging trap informational
how.snmp: SNMP traps: set {{host}}:{{trapPort}} as the trap receiver (v1 or v2c).

rules.title: Detections

auth_failure.desc: Five failed logins from the same device within five minutes.

config_change.name: Configuration changed
config_change.desc: A device logs that its configuration was changed (RouterOS "changed by", Cisco CONFIG_I; Linux sudo is not included).

restart.name: Device restarted
restart.desc: A restart or a shutdown reported by the device itself.

link.name: Link down / up
link.desc: A link that goes down (syslog or an SNMP linkDown trap) is an alert of the device until its link up arrives.

critical.name: Critical messages
critical.desc: Anything the device logs as critical, alert or emergency.

maint.title: Maintenance windows and escalation
maint.subtitle: Planned work is not an incident: in a maintenance window the alerts of the chosen devices are not sent to Central (or ServiceDesk) and are not escalated; they still show in the agent's own SOC queue, marked. An alert nobody has picked up is escalated.
maint.suppressedHint: Events muted by this window since the agent started

form.name: Name (e.g. Server room switch upgrade)
form.localTime: Times are in the agent's local time; a window may run past midnight.

quick.title: Mute now
quick.intro: A quick one-off window for chosen devices, e.g. before a restart.

esc.title: Escalation
esc.intro: An alert that stays new (nobody acknowledged, took or closed it) is escalated after the given minutes since it opened, separately for each severity.
esc.enabled: Escalate alerts nobody has picked up
esc.how: An escalation sends Central the event "SOC alert escalation" with the level (1, 2, 3...) in the "minimum count" field. Add rules for that event in Central -> Alerts: a rule with minimum count 1 notifies the first channel, minimum count 2 the next, and so on. Without such a rule the escalation is only visible in the SOC queue.

hostlogs.title: Security logs of the hosts
hostlogs.subtitle: The Windows Security log and the Linux authentication log of the managed hosts, read over WinRM and SSH (read only). Alerts come from them: repeated failed logons, a successful logon after attempts, an account lockout, a new account, a member added to a privileged group, the audit log cleared, a new service or task.
hostlogs.none: No managed Windows or Linux hosts.
hostlogs.note: Reading the Windows Security log needs an administrator account or the "Event Log Readers" group; a host where it fails shows the error. The first read goes back 15 minutes, later ones start where the previous one stopped. The agent does not keep the logs, only the counts, sources and names an alert needs.

traffic.title: Traffic analyzer
traffic.subtitle: Who talks to whom through a router, right now: the flows RouterOS Torch reports for the chosen interface, refreshed every few seconds. Nothing is changed on the router and the agent computer captures nothing.
traffic.noRouters: No MikroTik router with a stored credential - the analyzer asks the router (Torch).
traffic.ifacesFailed: The router did not return its interfaces - check the connection and the credential.

netmap.title: Whole-network map
netmap.subtitle: Gateway → routers → switches → computers, from what the devices themselves report (LLDP, MAC tables) - not guessed. Hover a node for details; double-click renames it.
netmap.centralIntro: The network map of the chosen client as its agent reported it (read-only; devices are renamed in the agent).
netmap.centralNoData: No agent has reported a network map yet.
netmap.partial: This is a first map from the database (assets and stored links). The full one - with the switches' ports and the subnets - is being built in the background and appears shortly.
netmap.renameHint: Double-click a node to rename it.
